verdict_text:
NO

The merge composes the two task vectors sequentially instead of taking both against the unmodified base: it computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1 - base)` and then `tmp + λ(ft2 - tmp)`, which expands to `(1-λ)·tmp + λ·ft2`, i.e. the second task vector is measured against the already-merged tensor. This violates "Required result" step 2, which mandates `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X] - base[X]) + λ(ft2[X] - base[X])`, and it is exactly the ordering hazard the specification calls out. The discrepancy is `λ²(ft1 - base)`, far above the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance for generic inputs, so the 48 merged tensors will fail grading. The other requirements (name-set and shared-tensor verification, merged count of 48, 114 output tensors, single output file) are correctly enforced.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
